text: Outside, at the foot of the dam spillway, hundreds of people are glued to their phones. One point two million just watched Mok try to kill Jaeha, live.
Inside, two minutes left. Lyra says leave the hunters; they came to kill him. Jaeha shakes his head. Everyone comes back. That's the only rule he has.

So everyone climbs at once. Borro takes five fresh minutes and hauls two unconscious hunters and Jaeha up one rope. Mok climbs the other with Nib's knife right below him, and Lyra covers the rest from the top.
Then a flooded passage, walls cracking, the light at the end shrinking. Nine seconds.
They burst out into the sunlight, every one of them: Borro carrying two hunters, Lyra herding four more, Nib walking Mok out at knifepoint, Yerin with Jaeha on her back.
Behind them, the gate snaps shut.
The crowd lowers their phones and stares. Then someone starts to clap.
And the whole spillway erupts.
Lyra drops her hunter and steps into the applause, bow high, braid flying. Thank you, yes, the arrow was hers.
Nib watches her with a flat stare.
Choi pushes through with four police officers. He called them the second that door closed. Is Jaeha alive?
Jaeha sits down hard on the wet concrete. Mostly, sir.
Mok finds his arrogance again and shouts for the cameras. The husk attacked his team. He has lawyers.
Then he leans down and whispers. His word against Jaeha's, and nobody believes a trap rat.
Jaeha keeps his polite smile. His eyes slide toward Borro.
Out of the moss, a little white drone with a pink ribbon lifts off, red light on.
The colour leaves Mok's face.
Bomi catches it and kisses it. It was in the moss the whole time, Mister Mok. Live. One point two million.
On her screen, a replay: Mok himself, slashing at Nib.
Black Hound's lawyer shoves through the crowd, yelling at Mok to say nothing.
Mok's jaw clenches. Sweat runs down his temple.
He forces a laugh. A fight inside a gate proves nothing about Gate 0912.
Jaeha stands, leaning on Yerin's arm, and asks politely if he may ask a few questions, the way he always did.
Mok sneers. Jaeha always did ask stupid questions.
The crowd goes quiet. At Gate 0912, the lamp over the boss door was red. Did Mok notice? Of course. He's led a hundred raids.
In the crowd, Choi's coffee stops halfway to his mouth.
Then why did his survey say C-grade? It wasn't his survey, Mok snaps. Kanghan paid for it.
The chat catches it. Kanghan, the core company? He knew the lamp was red and sent the kid in anyway. Keep asking.
So Jaeha does, softly, with Yerin gripping his arm. She was locked in too. Why close the door, knowing it would kill them?
Mok's pride answers. Because a red boss needs bait. That's what trap rats are for.
Total silence. A reporter's microphone shakes in his hand.
Jaeha nods, as if that makes sense, and asks the last one. Four years ago, at the Han River door, was Oh Minseok bait too?
Mok explodes. He followed orders. Kanghan told him to seal that door.
Then he hears what he just said.
One point six million. He said it. He said Kanghan. Clip it.
Mok stammers that it was an accident. It's in the report. Behind him, his lawyer clutches his head.
Jaeha lifts the orange phone. Then why keep it in his shield for four years?
Mok's lips move, but nothing comes out.
Nib answers for him. Insurance, in case his masters ever closed a door on him.
Bomi steers the drone up to the old screen. The whole country is watching. Play it.
One percent battery. One play. So everyone will watch it with him.
He presses play.
Darkness. Heavy breathing. A small light on wet stone and an orange sleeve.
Hundreds of screens show the same dark image. Nobody makes a sound.
Then Oh Minseok turns the camera on himself, sweating, laughing nervously. If the kid is watching this, he guesses he was right.
He glances over his shoulder and whispers. The survey was fake. The lamp is red. Mok's men are waiting at the door.
Jaeha watches, tears running through the blood on his face.
Minseok smiles that crooked grin. The kid goes out first today. No arguing.
Then his face fills the frame, serious now. If I don't come out, kid, it wasn't an accident.
The image freezes and breaks into blocks.
And the screen goes black. The battery is dead.
Nobody at the spillway moves.
Two million now, and the chat changes the word: not trap rat, trap-tester. Rest in peace, Oh Minseok.
A young hunter takes off his cap and holds it to his chest. Then another. Then a whole row.
Mok's legs give way, and he drops to his knees.
Jaeha limps up to him, for once the taller one. Mok spits: go on, hit me. Everyone's watching.
Jaeha doesn't raise a hand. Mok closed the door on Minseok. Jaeha won't close it on him. The police will.
Mok's face crumples, tears in the eyes that were dead.
The officers cuff him and lift him up, cameras flashing all along the line.
At the car, Mok looks back. Jaeha doesn't know what he's started. They'll bury him.
The door shuts on him.
And while every camera points at that car, Han Sora slips away up the wooded hill. Nobody watches her go.
At the same moment, in the rooftop room in Mangwon, Seoa cries with relief at her laptop. The landlady hugs her. Her brother's a hero now. He can keep the pets.
In Kanghan Tower, Director Baek watches the stream on a wall of screens, hands folded on his cane.
He touches his cane, and the screens go dark one by one.
He lifts a phone, the violet core glowing behind him, and smiles politely. Bury Black Hound. All of it. And find out what else that phone recorded.
